title: Characteristics of Spatial and Temporal Evolution of Land Subsidence in Langfang North Three Counties
content: Land subsidence is a typical slow geological hazard in the North China Plain. The north three counties of Langfang, Hebei Province, are adjacent to the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center. In recent years, with the acceleration of urbanization, the characteristics of land subsidence in the region have become complex and the spatiotemporal heterogeneity is significant. This study utilized PS-InSAR technology to monitor long-term ground subsidence in Langfang North Three Counties based on Envisat ASAR and Radarsat-2 time-series SAR images from 2003 to 2020, and validated the accuracy of the subsidence monitoring results using leveling data. An analysis of the factors influencing land subsidence was conducted by integrating groundwater level, land use and faults. The results show that the land subsidence in the North Three Counties exhibited a phased characteristic of first intensifying and then easing from 2003 to 2020. There were significant spatial distribution differences. The high-value subsidence areas were concentrated in the Yanjiao Town of Sanhe City. The points with an annual average subsidence rate exceeding 20 mm/a accounted for 18.98%. Long-term groundwater over-exploitation shows a strong association with ground subsidence, and the expansion of urban construction land is closely linked to the variation of subsidence. The Xiadian Fault and Jixian Foreland Fault exhibit apparent spatial correlation with the subsidence pattern. These findings hold significant implications for the prevention and control of urban land subsidence and the management of geological disaster risks in the North Three Counties.
